title: Euclid III.Def.1: Equal circles are those whose diameters are equal, or whose radii are equal.
summary: Euclid III.Def.1: Equal circles are those whose diameters are equal, or whose radii are equal.
body: Euclid, Book III, III.Def.1, as worded on this page: "Equal circles are those whose diameters are equal, or whose radii are equal." David E. Joyce's guide on the same page says: "This should not be a definition but a postulate or a theorem. The subject of the area of circles is developed in Proposition XII.2 and this definition is not used there. Instead the concept of equality, or rather, inequality is the same as it is in the rest of the Elements. For instance, if one figure is the contained in another, then the first is less than the other. Thus, there is a prior definition for the equality of two figures. Two circles are illustrated, namely circle BCD and circle…" Joyce describes his text as similar to Heath's translation of Heiberg, and slightly less literal.
said_by: Euclid, in David E. Joyce's text of the Elements at Clark University
